topic: animators using AI video generators getting lifeless motion, wrong timing, and characters that drift between shots
blind_spots: Most evidence is qualitative complaint; no quantitative data on failure rates, frequency, or how often these issues occur per generation.
Several key sonar-attributed quotes lack dates, making recency and trend direction hard to assess.
No evidence on which specific tools/models produce which failures—complaints are generic to 'AI video tools' rather than benchmarked per product.
Little to no evidence on workflow cost (time spent fixing drift/timing) or whether any prompting/post-fix techniques actually work at production quality.
The anatomical-error cluster comes from viewers identifying AI, not from animators describing their own production pain, so it may not reflect the professional-animator segment.
No evidence on audio/lip-sync, rendering cost, or rights/licensing pain points—scope is limited to motion, timing, and consistency.
contradictions: Movement is described both as 'very very slow movements' and as 'insanely jittery' within the same Corridor source, suggesting failure modes vary (too slow vs. too fast) rather than a single consistent timing defect.

The AtlasCloudAI post implies a prompt prefix can supply 'sakuga timing' and fix stiff/linear motion, which is in tension with sonar/critic claims that the lifeless-motion problem makes tools fundamentally 'unusable for professional-quality animation.'
